_about: When each data source is checked for a new release and how it is rebuilt (docs/automation.md, part 2). freshness.py reads it. probe: the cheap check (no data download). every_days: how often; hot_months: months when a release is expected, checked daily then. unit: what rebuilds it (units). review: 'auto' lets GitHub merge the rebuild's pull request when its checks pass; 'human' waits for a person. code_edit: a new period also needs a code change before the rebuild picks it up.

education.how: python education_series.py (where cache/education holds the earlier years)
education.why: On a clean runner it downloads every school year from the Urban Institute's API, which timed out (HTTP 524) after 13 minutes in a test on 2026-10-15.

infrastructure.how: python infrastructure_series.py --refresh; python power_plants.py --refresh; python transport_inventories.py --refresh

environment.why_ignore: environment_series.json's as_of is the month the files were downloaded, not a date of the data.

care.why: It needs cache/network/census_blocks_ids.json, which only the full build makes (test on 2026-10-15).

economy.how: python economy_series.py (delete the source's cache files first; see the source's note), then python federal_awards.py (federal money by function for the Public spending page), python federal_outlays.py --refresh (federal grants and contracts obligated and paid out), python unused_funds.py --refresh (federal grants that ended with an unpaid balance), python taken_back.py --refresh (federal grant money taken back), python cdbg_dr.py (disaster recovery subawards by municipio), python fema_pa_stage.py --refresh (FEMA Public Assistance by stage and age), python cdbg_regular.py (HUD's yearly CDBG by municipio) and python public_money_need.py (the Disaster funding and need page reads the FEMA series and the two CDBG files)

housing.how: python housing_series.py, python economy_series.py, python small_area.py, python women_labor.py, then python wcrp_rvi.py (the WCRP rebuild reads acs_barrio.json)

build.how: delete the source's cache file, then python build.py (the full build, about 3 GB of downloads)

osm.how: python roads.py, python gazetteer.py, then python build.py --refresh-network; python facilities.py --refresh osm (police stations); python community_assets.py --refresh townhall (city halls); python power_lines.py --refresh (transmission lines)

facilities.how: python facilities.py --refresh hud,usgs,usac (the police stations of OpenStreetMap are kept as published; renew them by hand with --refresh osm)

lihtc.how: Save https://www.huduser.gov/lihtc/lihtcpub.zip from a browser to cache/facilities/lihtcpub.zip (HUD USER refuses scripts; decision 71), then python facilities.py --only lihtc

wcrp.why: WCRP is a HUD CDBG-DR program: its files wait for Finance and Compliance review (HANDOFF), so a rebuild is run and reviewed by a person, never merged by itself.

conditions.how: python conditions.py --refresh, then python wcrp_rvi.py (the WCRP rebuild reads conditions_barrio.json)
conditions.why_ignore: wcrp_rvi_barrio.json's harvested is the day the runner read the original's ArcGIS services again (a clean runner has no cache), not a change of the data.
conditions.why_human: The WCRP index is rebuilt from conditions_barrio.json, so a new release of the local conditions changes it; WCRP is a HUD CDBG-DR program and its files are reviewed by a person (unit wcrp), so such a rebuild never merges by itself.

community.how: python community_assets.py --refresh nps,samhsa (the city halls of OpenStreetMap are kept as published; renew them by hand with --refresh townhall)

reservoirs.how: python reservoirs.py --refresh; python river_gauges.py --refresh; python groundwater.py --refresh; python rain_gauges.py --refresh

nightlights.how: python nightlights.py (needs EARTHDATA_TOKEN; docs/nightlights-setup.md); then python storm_recovery.py (no network) rebuilds the storm recovery files from the new monthly file

broadband.how: python broadband.py (needs FCC_BDC_USERNAME and FCC_BDC_HASH; docs/broadband.md)

fires.how: python fires.py --refresh (the last 12 months need FIRMS_MAP_KEY; docs/fires.md)

spending-pica.why: The program is a PDF read with pdftotext, which the clean runner does not have.

inflation.how: python inflation.py --refresh, then python docs/analysis/inflation-2026-11/make_page.py (the page's figures are written into it) and python i18n.py; raise js/i18n.js ?v= on inflation.html when its Spanish bundle changes
inflation.why: The page's text carries the latest month's figures, so a new month rewrites the page and its Spanish bundle, which a person checks before it is published.

credit.how: python credit.py --refresh (downloads the Summary of Deposits again and any HMDA year the cache does not hold)

drought.how: python drought.py --refresh (downloads every week again for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico, 79 requests)

essentials.how: python essentials.py --refresh (downloads the newest Overture places, about 130 MB, and Geofabrik's Puerto Rico extract, about 75 MB; the OpenStreetMap check needs osmium)

degrees.how: python degrees.py --refresh (downloads two IPEDS ZIP files a year, about 10 MB each, from NCES)

school_conditions.how: python school_conditions.py --refresh (Puerto Rico's all-students rows of three CRDC files a year from the Urban Institute's portal)

proficiency.how: python proficiency.py --refresh (Puerto Rico's all-students rows of the EDFacts assessment file, one a year, from the Urban Institute's portal)

providers.how: python providers.py --refresh (downloads the newest NPPES monthly file, about 1.1 GB, and keeps Puerto Rico's counts)

hexgrid.how: python hexgrid.py (no network: the census blocks, the building cache, flood.geojson and the caches of heat.py, vegetation.py and slope.py; run it after those)

netmig_age.how: python netmig_age.py --refresh (reads three Census Bureau CSV files, under 1 MB, and the UN's life tables, about 160 MB streamed and filtered to Puerto Rico)

jobs_reach.how: python jobs_reach.py --refresh (reads the Census Bureau's commuting flows, about 6 MB; needs scipy and the Overture places of cache/essentials; about 20 minutes)

cutoff.how: python cutoff.py (no download: reads roads.bin, flood.geojson, bridges.geojson, gazetteer.json and wcrp.geojson, and the census block cache; about a minute)

upstream.how: python upstream.py --refresh (reads EPA's wastewater plants and USGS's drainage areas, a few seconds; the rest is published layers and the census block cache)

sources.note: HUD USER refuses scripts, so no probe can read it: HUD adds a year each spring (the 2026-05-28 release covers 1987 to 2024). Check huduser.gov/portal/datasets/lihtc/property.html by hand; federal tax credit program, held for Compliance.

sources.name: USAC E-Rate entities (libraries)

sources.name: IRS exempt organizations (EO BMF, Puerto Rico)
EPA Toxics Release Inventory (Puerto Rico file)
sources.note: The newest reporting year with a Puerto Rico file; Envirofacts answers HEAD with an error, so the check asks for one byte. EPA's revisions of a year already read are picked up at the next rebuild of the unit.

sources.name: EPA Facility Registry Service (RMP and NPL)
sources.note: The counts of active RMP facilities and of final NPL sites in Puerto Rico: an edit that keeps both counts is missed until the next change.

sources.name: EPA ATTAINS assessment units (303(d) list)
sources.note: The layer's last edit date, for every state: a change elsewhere starts a rebuild that finds nothing new for Puerto Rico.

sources.name: EPA Green Book non-attainment areas (lead, sulfur dioxide)
sources.note: How many Puerto Rico areas are in non-attainment for lead and for sulfur dioxide: a redesignation changes a count.

sources.name: HUD CHAS by census tract (eGIS)
sources.note: The release (Date of Coverage) the eGIS item states; 2016-2020 on 2026-10-17, while HUD User has 2018-2022. HUD program data, and a new window moves every barrio estimate: a person checks it.

sources.name: NPS National Register of Historic Places (public locations)
sources.note: The layers have no edit date: the check counts Puerto Rico's points and polygons, so an edit that keeps both counts is missed until the next listing.

sources.name: SAMHSA National Directories of treatment facilities (N-SUMHSS)
sources.note: A new edition each year (the 2025 directories came out on 2026-03-06); the check reads the newest year the National Directories page names.

sources.name: USGS landslide susceptibility map of Puerto Rico (first author's tile copy at UPRM; the USGS release's DOI record)
sources.note: Two dates: the copy's last edit on ArcGIS Online (2019-11-01 on 2026-10-18) and the last update of the USGS data release's DOI record at DataCite (2021-08-18). The data release itself (ScienceBase) answers scripts with a bot check, so its record at DataCite is the scriptable sign of a new USGS version; the build still reads the copy, so a new USGS version needs the copy (or a direct file) to follow. A new map moves every barrio's figures: a person checks the rebuild.

sources.name: USGS Landsat 8 and 9 Collection 2 Level-2 surface temperature (Planetary Computer): the summer window of surface heat
sources.note: New Landsat scenes arrive every few days, but the published figures use the last three complete summers (June to September), so the data changes once a year, after September: the check turns in October. A new summer moves every barrio's figures, and the build checks the physics (San Juan hotter, Jayuya and Adjuntas cooler than Puerto Rico); a person reads the rebuild.

sources.name: Copernicus Sentinel-2 Level-2A, Collection 1 (Earth Search on AWS): the summer window of vegetation greenness
sources.note: New Sentinel-2 scenes arrive every few days, but the published figures use the last three complete summers (June to September), the window of surface heat, so the data changes once a year, after September: the check turns in October. A new summer moves every barrio's figures, and the build checks that San Juan is less green and Jayuya and Adjuntas greener than Puerto Rico, and that greener barrios are cooler in the heat file; a person reads the rebuild. Rebuild heat first.

sources.name: Overture Maps buildings theme: the newest monthly release
sources.note: Overture releases every month, so the probe turns almost every time; buildings change slowly, and the 3D view's 7 MB tile file is added again to the repository's history with each rebuild, so the check runs every 90 days. The same rebuild makes buildings_gap.pmtiles (buildings3d.py: 550,000 to 800,000 buildings at zoom 14, under 20 MB, none from OpenStreetMap). The build stops unless Puerto Rico has 1.9 to 2.5 million buildings, 99.5% of them fall in a barrio, San Juan is denser than Puerto Rico, 1% to 30% stand in a Special Flood Hazard Area, and buildings follow housing units across the barrios; a person reads the rebuild.

sources.name: NASA ECOSTRESS ECO_L2T_LSTE version 2 (LP DAAC, Earthdata login): the summer window of night surface heat
sources.note: ECOSTRESS passes several times a week at varying hours, but the published figures use the night passes of the last three complete summers (June to September), the window of surface heat, so the data changes once a year, after September: the check turns in October. The build needs the NASA Earthdata token (decisions 75 and 80) and checks that San Juan is warmer and Jayuya and Adjuntas cooler than Puerto Rico at night, and that the night is cooler than the morning in heat_series.json; a person reads the rebuild. Rebuild heat first.

sources.name: USGS reservoir levels, river flow, groundwater levels and rainfall (daily values and usual levels)
sources.note: The readings change every day and the page reads the latest live; the 120 daily values and usual levels of the four files (reservoirs, river gauges, groundwater wells, rain gauges) are rebuilt once a month.

sources.name: NWS flood stages of the river gauges (National Water Prediction Service)
sources.note: Read with the river gauges: the monthly rebuild of river_gauges.geojson asks NWS for each gauge's flood stages.

sources.name: NASA Black Marble VNP46A3 monthly night-time lights (LAADS DAAC)
sources.note: NASA adds a month about seven weeks after it ends; a monthly rebuild downloads only the months the cached summaries do not have (about 70 MB each). Needs the EARTHDATA_TOKEN secret, which expires about every 60 days (docs/nightlights-setup.md).

sources.name: FCC Broadband Data Collection: fixed broadband availability, June release
sources.note: Providers file as of June 30 and December 31; the FCC publishes a release some months later and republishes it as challenges settle. A monthly rebuild downloads only a June release the cache does not have. Needs the FCC_BDC_USERNAME and FCC_BDC_HASH secrets (docs/broadband.md).

sources.name: NASA FIRMS active fire detections (VIIRS on NOAA-20): yearly files and the last 12 months
sources.note: FIRMS adds detections every few hours, so the last 12 months move every day; a monthly rebuild keeps them current without a pull request a day. The yearly file of a finished year appears in the first months of the next. Needs the FIRMS_MAP_KEY secret for the last 12 months (docs/fires.md).

sources.name: OGP budget data sheets (Sábana)
sources.note: Public spending (decision 77): a proposed budget each spring and the approved one at the end of June. The check reads the newest budget folder linked from the home page; the rebuild reads every data sheet. The function crosswalk is a draft until the project lead reviews it.

sources.name: Planning Board four-year investment program (PICA)
sources.note: Public spending (decision 79): the Board adopts a new four-year program each year after public hearings. The check reads the newest adopted program linked from the home page; a person rebuilds where pdftotext is installed.

sources.name: DTRH consumer price index of Puerto Rico
sources.note: Monthly, about four weeks after the month; the indicadores.pr copy (CSV from 1984, basket weights) lags by months and is read only for 1999-2006.

sources.note: Designations come every ten years (2027-2036); Treasury can correct its file in between, under a new date in its name. A person checks the change before it is merged.

sources.note: The newest folder of the Bureau's metro-micro tables (2020 holds the 2016-2020 flows). A newer folder may hold a new release: a person checks it, changes the file's address and the period in transit_links.py and in the page's text, and rebuilds.
